rows.note: Use 入口 as the all-purpose noun for a designated entrance or access point, especially on signs or in public buildings.

example.english: The MTR station entrance is up ahead.
example.jyutping: dei6 tit3 zaam6 jap6 hau2 hai2 cin4 min6

rows.note: Use 門口 for the physical doorway or area immediately outside a home, shop, or building rather than a formal entrance point.

example.english: I’ll wait for you at the entrance.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 mun4 hau2 dang2 nei5

rows.note: Use 入場 for the act of entering a venue or event, especially when discussing admission or when someone makes an entrance there.

example.english: You can make your entrance ten minutes before the show starts.
example.traditional: 開場前十分鐘就可以入場。
example.jyutping: hoi1 coeng4 cin4 sap6 fan1 zung1 zau6 ho2 ji5 jap6 coeng4

rows.note: Use 入場資格 for the right or eligibility to enter, often established by a ticket, pass, or other requirement.

example.english: This ticket is your entrance pass.
example.jyutping: zoeng1 fei1 hai6 nei5 ge3 jap6 coeng4 zi1 gaak3
